outline: 1013 Angles in a Right Angle and Straight Line

examples.solution_text:
(a) Angles $11$ and $15$ occupy matching corners on the same side of the transversal: **corresponding**.

(b) Angles $13$ and $16$ are inside the two lines, on opposite sides of the transversal: **alternate**.

(c) Angles $14$ and $16$ are inside the two lines, on the same side of the transversal: **co-interior**.

These names describe positions even when the crossed lines are not parallel.

methods.description: Identify or locate corresponding angles by matching positions on the same side of the transversal, including non-parallel crossed lines.
Identify or locate alternate angles by checking that both are interior and on opposite sides of the transversal.
Identify or locate co-interior angles by checking that both are interior and on the same side of the transversal.
Apply the three positional tests to one indicated interior angle and list its partners in the requested order.

examples.derivation: The transversal intersects the upper line at (0.6, 1.2) and the lower line at approximately (-0.6383, -1.2766). Labels 11 and 15 occupy matching upper-left positions, so they are corresponding. Labels 13 and 16 are interior on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate. Labels 14 and 16 are interior on the same side, so they are co-interior. These positional classifications require no parallel-line assumption and match the supplied teaching and Foundation Q6.

The intersections are (0.6, 1.2) and (-0.6, -1.2). Angle 24 occupies the lower-right sector at the upper intersection. Its matching lower-right partner is 28; its opposite-side interior partner is 25; its same-side interior partner is 26. The solution arcs mark precisely these sectors: blue 243.435–360 degrees, green 63.435–180 degrees and purple 0–63.435 degrees. The ordered answer is 28, 25, 26, following the positional method used in Development Q7(b–d).
